You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Project a ray of the marker color inward from that bar at the marker's position until the marker; replace the marker cell with color 4 and stop. Transfer the same offset to the opposite parallel bar and project an inward ray from it in the opposite direction; if unobstructed it continues to the grid edge. Preserve both bars and other cells. Offsets are measured from the bar's start along its length (as with horizontal bars, marker offset 1 on bottom bar maps to offset 1 on top bar). Example 10x8: horizontal 7 bars at row0 cols0-2 and row9 cols4-6, marker 8 at (6,5): draw 8 down from top-bar offset1 at col1 through row9, draw 8 upward from bottom at col5 rows7-8, change marker (6,5) to4. Project the set of lane offsets onto both edge segments. From each marker segment, extend a ray inward, perpendicular to the edge, in the isolated-pixel color. A ray continues to the opposite edge if unobstructed; if it encounters an isolated pixel of that color, change that pixel to 4 and stop that ray there, leaving cells beyond it unchanged. Keep the edge markers as-is. Rays can extend all the way through the opposite edge row/column when unobstructed (do not stop just before the far boundary). Example: top marker at columns 13–16, bottom at 6–9; targets at columns 7,8,9 give offsets 1,2,3, thus lanes 14,15,16 from top and 7,8,9 from bottom.
